_comment: Hunt-package library: a LINK-ONLY index of the hunting queries in the PacktPublishing 'Advanced-Cyber-Threat-Intelligence-and-Hunting' companion repo, one entry per upstream query file, grouped by the ATT&CK tactic the hunt hypothesis tests (a technique can sit under several tactics; the tactic named is the one the hypothesis targets). No query text is copied: titles, hypotheses (ABLE form), method and false-positive notes are our own words, and the upstream_url is pinned to a commit. Every query is a STARTING POINT that must be mapped, unit-triggered and baselined in the consumer's own environment before any result is reported (workflows/wf-threat-analyst.md Phase 5, CAR rule). Baselines and lookups named under prerequisites come from the consumer's data, never from the upstream example values. attack_ids are verified against ATT&CK Enterprise at authoring time; an empty list plus attack_note means no id was recorded on purpose. telemetry uses CAR-style object/action strings (adaptation: cloudtrail/*, authentication/sign-in, kubernetes_audit/* extend the CAR objects). Hits are hunt leads for Phase 4, never attribution or same-operator edges. Read by humans only (no code loader).

initial-access._comment: Hunts for first access through exposed applications and external identities (ATT&CK TA0001).

entries.title: Per-host API request anomaly job (rare path, request burst, query-shape spread)
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: probing or exploiting an exposed API · L: internet-facing app hosts · E: web/API request logs show paths, volumes or query shapes the host has not served before
prerequisites: Elastic ML licence tier that runs anomaly-detection jobs
a derived per-request query-signature field the job partitions on
several days of request history before scores mean anything
entries.method: ml-anomaly (rare + high-count + high-distinct-count detectors per host)
entries.false_positive_notes: Releases, new client versions and scanners the consumer runs itself shift every detector; annotate deployments before reading anomalies.

entries.title: New cross-tenant (guest/external) sign-in relationships
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: access through an external or partner identity · L: identity tenant · E: successful sign-ins whose home tenant differs from the resource tenant, first seen inside the last week
prerequisites: Entra ID sign-in logs retained for at least 30 days
entries.false_positive_notes: Newly onboarded partners, contractors and B2B collaboration produce exactly this shape; check against the partner onboarding record.

execution._comment: Hunts for adversary code first running on a host or cloud runtime (TA0002).

entries.title: Web-server process spawns a shell shortly after a script POST
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: a planted web shell runs operator commands · L: IIS/PHP servers · E: a POST to a script path followed within minutes by the web-server worker starting a command shell or PowerShell
prerequisites: web request telemetry and endpoint process telemetry joined on the same host identifier
entries.method: sequence (request then child process, per host, short max-span)
entries.false_positive_notes: Admin consoles and build hooks that shell out legitimately; the upstream exclusion list of known upload endpoints must be replaced with the consumer's own.

entries.title: Disk-image mount followed by script-host launching a shortcut or script
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: payload delivered in an ISO/IMG to dodge mark-of-the-web · L: user workstations · E: an image file opened or mounted, then a script host runs a shortcut or script from the new volume
prerequisites: file-open/mount events (not only file creation) from the endpoint sensor
entries.method: sequence (mount then script-host execution, per host and user)
entries.false_positive_notes: Software installers and IT tooling distributed as disk images; vendor ISOs opened by administrators.

entries.title: PowerShell launched with an encoded command argument
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: hiding PowerShell intent behind base64 · L: endpoints · E: process command lines carrying the encoded-command switch or its abbreviations
entries.false_positive_notes: Management agents and deployment tools encode commands routinely; baseline the parent process and signer before triage.

entries.title: PowerShell download-and-invoke primitives on the command line
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: one-liner that fetches and runs a second stage · L: endpoints · E: command lines combining web-request and invoke-expression primitives
entries.false_positive_notes: Package bootstrap scripts and admin automation use the same primitives; the short alias match is very noisy without a parent/user filter.

entries.title: PowerShell file activity inside the user temp directory
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: loader drops and runs follow-on content from temp · L: endpoints · E: PowerShell file events under the per-user temp path
entries.false_positive_notes: Installers and update helpers stage in temp constantly; useful mainly as a pivot from another hit, not standalone.

entries.title: Scheduled task created and deleted within a minute
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: one-shot execution through a throwaway task · L: Windows hosts · E: task-created then task-deleted security events for the same task name within one minute
prerequisites: Windows object-access auditing that emits task create/delete security events
entries.method: sequence (create then delete, same task name)
entries.false_positive_notes: Software deployment and remote-management tools create transient tasks; record the creating account and task path.

entries.title: Service installed, started and removed within a minute
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: single-use service for SYSTEM execution · L: Windows hosts · E: service install, start and stop/delete system events on one service name inside a minute
prerequisites: System event log collection including service control manager events
entries.method: sequence (install, start, removal; same service name)
entries.false_positive_notes: Remote admin suites and some patching tools use the same lifecycle; check the image path and installing account.

entries.title: One principal exercising several serverless create/update/permission actions
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: deploying a serverless backdoor · L: cloud account · E: a principal performing two or more of function create, code update, permission add and trigger mapping
prerequisites: CloudTrail management events ingested for the relevant regions
entries.false_positive_notes: CI/CD deploy roles do this on every release; exclude by role, not by principal name alone.

persistence._comment: Hunts for footholds that survive reboot or re-login: autostarts, services, Office macros, web shells (TA0003).

entries.title: High-entropy POST bodies to script endpoints
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: delivering or driving an obfuscated web shell · L: internet-facing web servers · E: short POST bodies with high Shannon entropy sent to script extensions
entries.platform: Generic (Sigma; convert to the consumer's SIEM backend)
prerequisites: request-body entropy and length fields computed at ingest (not native to most web logs)
entries.false_positive_notes: Legitimate binary or compressed uploads and API clients that send encoded payloads; allowlist by path and client.

entries.title: Outlook VBA project file written by a process other than Outlook
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: mail-client macro persistence · L: user profiles · E: create/modify events on the Outlook VBA project file from a non-Outlook process
entries.method: signature-match on path with process exclusion
entries.false_positive_notes: Profile migration and backup/restore tools rewrite the file.

entries.title: Fleet-wide rarity of Run/RunOnce values
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: autostart persistence · L: a defined workstation peer group · E: Run/RunOnce values present on very few hosts
prerequisites: host type and fleet tag fields populated so the stack runs within one peer group
entries.method: rarity-baseline (stack count by host count, ascending)
entries.false_positive_notes: Department-specific software and freshly rolled-out agents are rare at first; re-run after deployments settle.

entries.title: Run/RunOnce value that invokes a script engine or shell
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: autostart through a script interpreter · L: Windows endpoints · E: registry autostart values naming a shell or script host
entries.platform: Generic (Sigma; convert to the consumer's SIEM backend)
entries.method: signature-match on key path and value content
entries.false_positive_notes: Logon scripts and some vendor helpers call a shell directly.

entries.title: Run/RunOnce value pointing into a user- or world-writable directory
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: autostart of a dropped binary · L: Windows endpoints · E: autostart values whose target sits under profile, public, program-data, temp or download paths
entries.false_positive_notes: Per-user installers (chat, meeting and sync clients) autostart from the profile by design.

entries.title: Rare service name and image-path pairs across the fleet
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: persistence via a new Windows service · L: Windows estate · E: service-install events whose name/path pair appears on five or fewer hosts in 30 days
prerequisites: 30 days of service-install events from both the security and system logs
entries.false_positive_notes: Driver installs, niche line-of-business software and pilot rollouts.

entries.title: Word global template modified by a shell or script host
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: template-macro persistence · L: user profiles · E: file events on the global Word template from a shell or script interpreter
entries.platform: Generic (Sigma; convert to the consumer's SIEM backend)
entries.method: signature-match on path and writing process
entries.false_positive_notes: User customisation, Office repair and enterprise template-distribution scripts.

privilege-escalation._comment: Hunts for gaining higher integrity, SYSTEM or broader cloud/cluster rights (TA0004).

entries.title: Low/medium-integrity process calling injection APIs on a high/system process
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: injecting into a more privileged process · L: endpoints · E: memory/thread API calls from low or medium integrity into high or system integrity targets, rare by host count
prerequisites: endpoint sensor that records API-call events with source and target integrity levels
entries.method: rarity-baseline (keep combinations seen on few hosts)
entries.false_positive_notes: Security products, accessibility tools and debuggers cross integrity levels legitimately.

entries.title: Trusted signed process loading an unsigned or foreign-signed DLL outside system folders
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: DLL hijack/side-load under a trusted binary · L: endpoints · E: one-off library loads where the host process is trusted-signed but the DLL is not, from a non-system path
prerequisites: library-load telemetry with code-signature fields for both process and DLL
entries.false_positive_notes: Third-party plug-ins and shell extensions load into signed hosts everywhere; the upstream process exclusion list is environment-specific.

entries.title: Low/medium-integrity parent whose child runs as SYSTEM
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: UAC bypass or token elevation · L: endpoints · E: a process start at low or medium integrity followed by a SYSTEM-integrity child within minutes
prerequisites: process events carrying integrity level and stable process entity ids
entries.false_positive_notes: Installers and elevation brokers that hand off to SYSTEM services.

entries.title: Remote thread creation with common benign sources filtered
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: code injection through a remote thread · L: Windows endpoints with Sysmon · E: remote-thread events outside the known WMI and session-manager noise
entries.platform: Generic (Sigma; convert to the consumer's SIEM backend)
prerequisites: Sysmon with remote-thread events enabled
entries.false_positive_notes: Endpoint security, game anti-cheat and accessibility software create remote threads.

entries.title: Cloud principal attaching or putting a policy on itself
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: identity granting itself more permissions · L: cloud account · E: policy attach/put calls where caller and target identity match
prerequisites: CloudTrail IAM management events
entries.false_positive_notes: Bootstrap automation and break-glass roles; the substring caller/target match can also collide on similar names.

entries.title: Privileged or host-PID pod creation in a managed cluster
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: container deployed to reach the node · L: managed Kubernetes clusters · E: pod-create audit records with a privileged security context or host PID namespace
prerequisites: Kubernetes API audit logs shipped to the workspace with request bodies
entries.false_positive_notes: Node agents, CNI/CSI drivers and monitoring daemonsets run privileged by design; allowlist by namespace and image.

defense-evasion._comment: Hunts for proxy execution, in-memory staging and audit-log tampering (TA0005).

entries.title: 30-day per-host baseline of living-off-the-land binary invocations
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: proxy execution through built-in binaries · L: endpoints · E: binary/command pairs never or rarely seen on that host in the last 30 days
prerequisites: a continuously running transform writing a baseline index that downstream rules query
30 days of process-start events
entries.method: rarity-baseline (continuous transform producing a first-seen lookup)
entries.false_positive_notes: Admin scripts and software updates introduce new command lines in bursts; the lookup only helps once it covers a quiet period.

entries.title: Committed read-write-execute memory allocations outside known JIT processes
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: in-memory shellcode staging · L: endpoints with the XDR memory table · E: RWX commit allocations by processes that are not known JIT runtimes
prerequisites: an XDR tier that exposes memory-allocation events
entries.false_positive_notes: JIT runtimes, browsers, IDEs and some games allocate RWX pages; extend the exclusion set from the consumer's data.

entries.title: Cloud audit trail stopped, deleted or narrowed
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: turning off cloud audit logging · L: cloud account · E: successful stop/delete/update trail or event-selector changes
prerequisites: CloudTrail delivered to an independent store so tampering is still recorded
entries.false_positive_notes: Planned logging re-architecture and trail consolidation; confirm against the change record.

credential-access._comment: Hunts for stolen sessions, tokens, hashes and keys, mostly identity-plane telemetry (TA0006).

entries.title: Sign-in and Graph activity in one session from different source IPs
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: adversary-in-the-middle token theft and replay · L: identity provider and Graph API · E: one session id whose sign-in and Graph calls arrive from different IPs within minutes
prerequisites: sign-in logs and Graph activity logs both ingested with session identifiers
entries.false_positive_notes: Mobile clients roaming between networks, split-tunnel VPNs and IPv4/IPv6 dual stack produce two IPs per session.

entries.title: Repeated MFA denials followed by a successful sign-in
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: push-bombing until the user accepts · L: identity tenant · E: three or more MFA denials in a short bucket then a success for the same user
prerequisites: Entra ID sign-in logs with MFA result codes
entries.false_positive_notes: Users fumbling a new authenticator or lost-device scenarios; ask the user before escalating.

entries.title: New delegated OAuth permission grants
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: illicit consent grant for long-lived app access · L: identity tenant · E: directory audit records of new OAuth permission grants
prerequisites: Entra ID audit logs
an approved-application inventory to diff against
entries.method: enumeration (every grant reviewed against an approved-app list)
entries.false_positive_notes: Every legitimate app consent appears; the hunt value is the review against an approved-application inventory.

entries.title: One source IP failing against many distinct users
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: password spraying · L: identity tenant · E: invalid-credential failures from one IP across more than ten distinct users in a day
prerequisites: Entra ID sign-in logs with failure codes
entries.false_positive_notes: Shared egress IPs (corporate NAT, proxies) and misconfigured service accounts.

entries.title: One successful session id seen from more than one IP
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: stolen session cookie replayed elsewhere · L: identity tenant · E: successful sign-ins sharing a session id across distinct IPs
prerequisites: Entra ID sign-in logs with session identifiers
entries.false_positive_notes: Network roaming, mobile carriers and dual-stack clients; weigh geography and user-agent change alongside IP count.

entries.title: Direct reads of the SAM or SECURITY registry hives
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: offline hash or LSA-secret extraction · L: Windows endpoints and servers · E: registry query/open on SAM or SECURITY hives from unexpected processes
prerequisites: registry read/open auditing (often not on by default)
entries.false_positive_notes: Backup agents and some security tools read these hives.

entries.title: LSASS memory dump through the built-in minidump export
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: credential dumping with a signed system DLL · L: Windows endpoints · E: rundll32 command lines combining the system minidump DLL with a full-dump argument
entries.platform: Generic (Sigma; convert to the consumer's SIEM backend)
entries.false_positive_notes: Rare; vendor crash-diagnostics scripts occasionally use the same export.

entries.title: Certificate export commands on federation servers
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: stealing the federation token-signing key to forge SAML tokens · L: federation servers · E: shell command lines exporting PFX certificates
entries.false_positive_notes: Certificate renewal and migration work by PKI administrators.

entries.title: Instance-role credentials used from more than two source IPs
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: instance-metadata credential theft and reuse · L: cloud compute roles · E: assumed-role sessions issued to compute roles appearing from several IPs
prerequisites: CloudTrail with session issuer fields
a role naming convention or tag that identifies compute instance roles
entries.false_positive_notes: Autoscaling groups and NAT/VPC-endpoint egress can legitimately present several IPs; the upstream role-name patterns are naming-convention specific.

discovery._comment: Hunts for filesystem walks and cloud reconnaissance ahead of collection (TA0007).

entries.title: Process listing hundreds of distinct directories in minutes
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: scripted filesystem walk ahead of collection · L: file servers and endpoints · E: more than 500 distinct directory listings from one process inside five minutes
prerequisites: an endpoint sensor that emits directory-listing events (uncommon by default)
entries.method: threshold (distinct directories in a time window)
entries.false_positive_notes: Backup, indexing, antivirus scans and sync clients walk trees constantly.

entries.title: IAM API actions a principal used three times or fewer in 30 days
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: cloud identity reconnaissance or one-off manipulation · L: cloud account · E: per-principal IAM actions with very low 30-day counts
prerequisites: 30 days of CloudTrail IAM events
entries.false_positive_notes: Administrators doing occasional IAM housekeeping; new principals are rare in everything.

entries.title: Principal-to-bucket access relationship first seen in the last week
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: a principal discovering and touching storage it never used · L: object storage · E: principal/bucket pairs whose first access falls in the recent window
prerequisites: S3 data events enabled (they are not logged by default)
entries.false_positive_notes: New applications, new team members and data-platform migrations.

lateral-movement._comment: Hunts for movement between hosts, directory objects and cloud accounts (TA0008).

entries.title: Computer account writing the resource-based delegation attribute
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: resource-based constrained delegation abuse · L: Active Directory · E: directory-change events on the delegation attribute initiated by a machine account
prerequisites: directory-service change auditing on the relevant OUs
entries.method: signature-match on attribute and actor type
entries.false_positive_notes: Some provisioning flows write the attribute legitimately, usually from a user/service account rather than a machine account.
entries.attack_note: No technique id recorded on purpose: map the follow-on (delegated ticket request and use) to the live ATT&CK matrix before writing it on the hunt record.

entries.title: Executable written by the kernel SMB path then executed within seconds
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: remote execution with a binary pushed over admin shares · L: Windows servers and workstations · E: an executable created by the System process followed by its execution within ten seconds
prerequisites: file-creation events attributed to the System process
entries.method: sequence (write then execute, same host and path)
entries.false_positive_notes: Software distribution systems and remote admin tools behave identically; allowlist by source host.

entries.title: New cross-account role assumptions
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: pivoting through delegated trust between cloud accounts · L: multi-account organisation · E: successful role assumptions where source and target accounts differ, first seen in the last week
prerequisites: CloudTrail from every account in scope (an organisation trail)
entries.false_positive_notes: New account vending, cross-account CI pipelines and audit tooling.

collection._comment: Hunts for bulk gathering and staging of data on disk, shares and object storage (TA0009).

entries.title: Recursive bulk-copy utilities and copy-to-UNC
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: bulk gathering of files ahead of exfiltration · L: endpoints and file servers · E: recursive copy-utility or copy-to-share command lines, ranked by volume
entries.false_positive_notes: Backups, migrations and profile sync use the same switches.

entries.title: Recursive searches filtered on document, mailbox or secret keywords
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: hunting for documents and credentials on disk · L: endpoints · E: recursive listing commands combined with sensitive extension or secret keywords
entries.false_positive_notes: Developers and administrators searching for config files; e-discovery tooling.

entries.title: One process reading hundreds of files in minutes
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: scripted document harvesting · L: endpoints and file servers · E: more than 500 file reads across many paths by one process inside ten minutes
prerequisites: file-read events from the endpoint sensor
entries.false_positive_notes: Antivirus, backup, search indexers and build systems; file-read telemetry is often sampled or off.

entries.title: Account touching many SMB shares across many hosts in a day
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: share sweeping for data · L: file servers · E: one user accessing more than ten distinct shares on more than three hosts in 24 hours
prerequisites: UNC-path file events or file-server share-access auditing
entries.method: threshold (distinct shares and hosts per user)
entries.false_positive_notes: Service accounts for backup, inventory and vulnerability scanning.

entries.title: Burst of file writes into common staging directories
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: local staging before exfiltration · L: endpoints and servers · E: more than 250 writes in ten minutes into temp, public, program-data, perf-log or recycle-bin paths
entries.method: threshold (writes per directory in a time window)
entries.false_positive_notes: Installers, updaters and log rotation write heavily into these paths.

entries.title: Principal retrieving more than 100 objects from one bucket in an hour
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: bulk retrieval from cloud object storage · L: object storage · E: hourly per-principal per-bucket object-get counts above threshold
prerequisites: S3 data events enabled
entries.false_positive_notes: Analytics jobs, replication and backup roles; compare distinct-key counts with the role's normal pattern.

command-and-control._comment: Hunts for callback channels. The rarity entries are the Chapter 12 C2 patterns: few-hosts-heavy DNS, globally-rare/locally-noisy user agents, URI reuse across domains (TA0011).

entries.title: Very high query volume against one parent domain
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: DNS tunnelling for C2 or exfiltration · L: resolvers and endpoints · E: query counts against a single parent domain far above its normal volume
entries.platform: Generic (Sigma; convert to the consumer's SIEM backend)
prerequisites: DNS logs with a derived parent/registrable-domain field
entries.false_positive_notes: CDNs with dynamic subdomains, telemetry-over-DNS products and anti-malware lookups.

entries.title: Host/process/destination tuple seen on exactly one day: today
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: new external callback destination · L: Windows endpoints · E: outbound connection tuples absent from a 30-day history and first appearing today
prerequisites: 30 days of Sysmon network-connection events
a DNS lookup to name destinations
internal address ranges defined for exclusion
entries.false_positive_notes: Software updates and new SaaS adoption; needs a reverse-DNS or passive-DNS lookup to be triageable.

entries.title: Narrow-band average inter-event interval per host/process/destination
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: periodic beaconing over web ports · L: endpoints · E: non-browser process streams with at least eight events and a sub-hour average interval
prerequisites: network events attributed to process name
entries.method: periodicity (average interval; adaptation: add jitter/variance before trusting it)
entries.false_positive_notes: Update checkers, telemetry agents and chat clients beacon by design.

entries.title: Domains resolved by at most two hosts but heavily
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: implant calling a dedicated callback domain · L: a workstation peer group · E: non-browser lookups for a domain from very few hosts with high total volume
prerequisites: endpoint DNS events with the querying process
host type and fleet tag fields
entries.method: rarity-baseline (low host count with high volume)
entries.false_positive_notes: Developer tools, niche licence servers and pilots; the two-label domain extraction mis-handles multi-label public suffixes.

entries.title: Seven-day global frequency table of proxy user agents
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: custom client tooling · L: web proxy · E: the global count for every user-agent string, used as the rarity reference for the paired query
prerequisites: 7 days of proxy logs
a lookup index to hold the output
entries.false_positive_notes: Not a detector on its own; a baseline window that already contains the implant hides it.

entries.title: User agents rare globally but noisy from one source
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: a bespoke client calling a few destinations · L: web proxy · E: a user agent with fewer than ten 7-day sightings fleet-wide but more than fifty in 24 hours from one source
prerequisites: the user-agent rarity lookup produced by pk-ch12-ua-global-frequency
entries.method: rarity-baseline (global rarity joined to local volume)
entries.false_positive_notes: Single-host appliances, scanners and scripted integrations with custom agent strings.

entries.title: Identical URI requested across three or more destination domains
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: shared C2 or kit path across rotating domains · L: web proxy · E: the same path-plus-query seen on at least three domains with at least twenty requests
prerequisites: proxy logs with full path and query
entries.false_positive_notes: Generic paths (favicon, health checks, analytics beacons, CDN assets) recur across domains; suppress them first.

exfiltration._comment: Hunts for data leaving the estate: byte asymmetry and baseline-vs-recent shifts in duration, frequency and volume (TA0010).

entries.title: Source/destination pairs sending far more than they receive
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: data leaving the network · L: egress · E: outbound/inbound byte ratio above five with more than 50 MB out over repeated sessions
prerequisites: flow records with both byte directions
entries.false_positive_notes: Backups to cloud, video upload, code pushes and log shipping.

entries.title: Recent session durations five times the prior baseline
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: long-running tunnel where short sessions were normal · L: egress · E: per-tuple recent average duration far above the preceding six-day average
prerequisites: 7 days of flow records with session duration
entries.false_positive_notes: Software changes that switch to persistent connections (websockets, long-poll).

entries.title: Daily session counts three times the prior baseline
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: periodic transfer channel emerging · L: egress · E: per-tuple daily session count well above its baseline daily average and above one hundred
prerequisites: 7 days of flow records
entries.false_positive_notes: New integrations, monitoring probes and retry storms after an outage.

entries.title: Per-pair daily outbound volume baseline for servers
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: (baseline builder) normal server egress · L: server segment · E: average, max and spread of daily outbound bytes per source/destination pair
prerequisites: host type field identifying servers
a lookup index to hold the output
entries.false_positive_notes: Not a detector; a baseline window that already contains exfiltration normalises it.

entries.title: Today's server egress three times its daily baseline
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: large-volume exfiltration from servers · L: server segment · E: today's outbound bytes per pair above three times baseline and above 10 MB
prerequisites: the daily-volume baseline lookup produced by pk-ch13-volume-baseline
entries.false_positive_notes: Month-end jobs, re-syncs and disaster-recovery tests.

impact._comment: Hunts for encryption, wiping, recovery inhibition, mass account lockout and unauthorised OT controller work (TA0040).

entries.title: Process modifying or renaming more than 1,000 files in five minutes
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: ransomware encryption · L: endpoints and file servers · E: per-process modify/overwrite/rename bursts across many directories
entries.method: threshold (file changes in a time window)
entries.false_positive_notes: Archivers, build systems, sync clients and bulk renames by administrators.

entries.title: One subject resetting or disabling more than 100 accounts in ten minutes
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: destructive mass password reset or disablement · L: Active Directory · E: account reset/disable/change events by one subject across many targets
prerequisites: account-management auditing on domain controllers
entries.method: threshold (distinct targets per subject in a time window)
entries.false_positive_notes: Identity-governance jobs and scheduled deprovisioning runs.

entries.title: Process opening raw physical-drive or volume devices
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: disk wiping or boot-record overwrite · L: endpoints and servers · E: file events against raw device paths
prerequisites: sensor coverage of raw device handles
entries.false_positive_notes: Disk imaging, encryption, backup and forensic tools.

entries.title: Shadow-copy deletion via built-in utilities
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: inhibiting recovery before encryption · L: Windows hosts · E: command lines deleting volume shadow copies through the standard utilities
entries.false_positive_notes: Backup software rotating its own snapshots and disk-space cleanup scripts.

entries.title: PLC engineering software launched outside a maintenance window
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: unauthorised controller programming · L: engineering workstations in the OT zone · E: rare executions of PLC engineering software with no matching maintenance window
prerequisites: a maintenance-window lookup table keyed by workstation
endpoint telemetry from the OT engineering segment
entries.false_positive_notes: Emergency maintenance not recorded in the window table; vendor support sessions.
entries.attack_note: ICS-matrix behaviour; record a technique id only after checking the live ATT&CK for ICS matrix.

cross-tactic-ttb._comment: Time-Terrain-Behavior (TTB) entity scoring: technique-agnostic, so attack_ids is empty by design. Chapter 15 is the base multiplicative diversity score; Chapter 18 adds the velocity ratio against peer-group baselines for machine-speed or agentic activity. A high score is a triage lead, never a detection or attribution.

entries.title: Time-Terrain-Behavior diversity per host
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: an entity operating across unusually many time contexts, sensors and action types · L: whole estate · E: per-host distinct counts of time, terrain and behaviour categories
prerequisites: 30 days of mixed telemetry carrying module/dataset and category fields so events can be bucketed
entries.false_positive_notes: Servers, jump hosts and admin workstations are broad by role; compare within peer groups, not fleet-wide.

entries.title: Drill-down of one entity's Time-Terrain-Behavior mix
entries.hypothesis: A: any · B: (triage) explain why one entity scored high · L: one entity · E: event counts per time/terrain/behaviour combination
prerequisites: the bucket definitions from pk-ch15-ttb-diversity
entries.false_positive_notes: The upstream file elides the classification logic and points back to the scoring query; reuse the same bucket definitions or the two will disagree.

entries.title: Velocity-extended Time-Terrain-Behavior score against peer-group baselines
entries.hypothesis: A: any (incl. automated or agentic tooling) · B: an entity crossing time contexts far faster than its peers · L: whole estate by peer group · E: transition rate relative to the peer-group median, folded into the TTB product
prerequisites: host-to-peer-group enrich policy populated from the consumer's asset inventory
peer-group baseline enrich policy holding median transition rates computed from the consumer's own known-clean window
30 days of mixed telemetry
entries.method: diversity-score with velocity ratio vs peer-group median
entries.false_positive_notes: Batch jobs, CI runners and monitoring agents are machine-speed by design; a peer group that mixes them with workstations makes every workstation look slow.
